title: Nebula Telecom - Procurement: MSA / DPA / SLAs / Pricing / Onboarding
summary: Procurement and legal working session to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing approvals, and next steps for vendor onboarding. Discussed hosted vs private deployment, KMS/encryption, SOC2 evidence, and procurement timeline. Action items assigned for redlines, SOC2 upload, and scheduling CISO call.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-18
- Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Claire (Nebula Procurement), Marcus (Nebula Legal), Ibrahim (Nebula Security), Dana (Nebula AI Platform), Owen (Nebula Infra)

Summary (auto):
Quick procurement/ legal sync to unblock PO and pilot. Went through MSA high level redlines, DPA expectations for customer data, SLA percentiles and credits, and the preferred procurement flow. Agreed to exchange documents and schedule a security deep dive.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Let's do quick intros, then we'll jump into the MSA and DPA items. We have about 50 minutes, so want to be efficient.
00:12 Claire: Hi all, Claire from procurement, Marcus from legal, Ibrahim from security. We'll be taking point on the redlines.
00:22 Marcus: Hi, yes thanks. We circulated an initial redline but it's mostly high level, we want to cover SLAs and liability caps.
00:30 Lina: Great. I'll help on the technical implications of the SLAs and deployment options. Quick note, our dedicated product is Redwood Dedicated, we also support private VPC installs for on-prem but there are slightly different onboarding steps.
00:45 Ibrahim: For us security is key — data residency, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS support, HSM for keys if needed, audit logs, SSO / SAML integration, RBAC.
00:59 Samir: Understood. On the MSA we usually accept most standard enterprise redlines but two things often come up: SLA uptime percentage and the data processing terms in the DPA. We'll want to align on who's the data controller vs processor and subprocessors list.
01:15 Marcus: On liability we're looking at caps that are standard for telecom contracts. The bigger ask is around indemnity and security breach notifications, specific timing for notification and forensic support.
01:27 Dana: From the platform side we'll need to run a small pilot to validate latency/cost for our traffic shape — mostly short chat-style queries and some batch embedding jobs. If redswood can provide benchmark results for an equivalent workload that'd be helpful.
01:41 Lina: We can run a two-week Dedicated pilot — provision a reserved pool with the kernels optimized for your model class. Note: sometimes transcription in our docs says K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry for the spelling, but we will ensure the caching behavior is documented.
01:56 Owen: Hosting model-wise, are you offering hosted API or do we need VPC? For telecom regs, some traffic must remain in-eu or regional.
02:07 Samir: You can do hosted with region pinning, or dedicated in your VPC. For FIPS/HSM or air-gapped needs we also support Private/on-prem but that's a longer timeline.
02:20 Ibrahim: We need KMS integration with our cloud provider, and ability to rotate keys. Also will need SOC2 Type II and recent pen test results.
02:32 Lina: We'll share SOC2 Type II and our security pack. For KMS we integrate with major providers; for HSM we have partners. There may be some small integration engineering work.
02:44 Marcus: On the DPA we'd like processor audit rights and a clause for data deletion on contract termination. Also need clarity on sub-processors and where logs are stored.
02:56 Samir: That's standard. We'll attach the subprocessor list and retention schedules. We can accept deletion clauses with reasonable notice windows.
03:08 Claire: Procurement question — pricing approval. We need a committed capacity discount tier and an estimated monthly cost for a 6-month pilot. Also PO terms net-45 is preferred.
03:22 Samir: We can provide committed capacity tiers and a pricing sheet. Our usual enterprise terms are net-30 but we can look at net-45 for larger committeds. We'll also show cost modeled with batching and caching recommendations to reduce unit costs.
03:36 Marcus: SLAs — we need 99.9% uptime and credits for below that; also response time SLOs for p95 and p99 for small and medium payloads.
03:48 Lina: Technically we guarantee availability for Dedicated with SLA; for hosted API we have different SLOs. For p95/p99 latency we need to confirm numbers because it depends on model size, quantization, and sequence length. For example, small-chat model under dedicated pool usually p95 ~110ms and p99 ~220ms for 512 token context, but that's illustrative.
04:12 Ibrahim: We need an explicit guarantee on log retention and encrypted at rest, and access controls — who can access logs. Also audit logs for admin actions.
04:25 Samir: We'll include RBAC doc and audit log retention table. We also keep per-route tracing hooks in the console for observability.
04:36 Dana: On onboarding, we'll need a runbook: test accounts, test data, evaluation prompts and acceptance criteria. We'll hand you success criteria but want Redwood to instrument cost/latency dashboards.
04:50 Ravi: That's part of CSM onboarding — we'll set up the console and dashboard and run an initial quality check against your eval set.
05:00 Claire: Timeline — procurement aims to have vendor signed by end of July if legal approves. Do you have legal support that can take quick redlines?
05:12 Samir: Yes, our legal team can turn on redlines within 3 business days once we get the initial set. We usually try to close procurement within 2 weeks after redlines.
05:22 Marcus: We'll send a consolidated redline doc today. Expect a few edits on indemnity and SLA credits.
05:29 Samir: Perfect. We'll review and push back on any unacceptable items. Also we'll add a table for SLA credits in the MSA appendix.
05:37 Ibrahim: One more on data residency: some logs may cross region for processing, we need assurance logs for EU data remain in EU.
05:47 Lina: We can do region pinning for logging and storage; for some managed features there may be limited metadata that crosses regions but we'll document that specifically.
05:58 Claire: Procurement wants to know the billing contact and contract signing flow: will Redwood accept e-sign via DocuSign and PO?
06:10 Samir: Yes, DocuSign is fine. We accept PO and can invoice net-30 or net-45 as agreed. Billing contact will be in the pricing worksheet.
06:20 Dana: On the pilot, can you guarantee no throttling/cold starts that would skew our latency tests?
06:29 Lina: For the Dedicated pilot we will reserve capacity to avoid cold starts; for best results we'll warm the model and provide KV cache warmup scripts. Note that some runtime optimizations — kernel selection, quantization — depend on the model binary.
06:46 Owen: Any references or customers in telecom? We prefer references to validate throughput patterns.
06:52 Samir: We have a couple of telco customers (we'll share non-confidential case studies). Also we can run a tailored benchmark using a representative subset of your traffic.
07:04 Marcus: Regarding DPA, one redline we have is breach notification within 48 hours; is that feasible?
07:11 Samir: We commit to prompt notification but forensic timelines vary; typical wording is "promptly and within 72 hours" — we can escalate internally to see if 48 is feasible for your case, pending legal approval.
07:27 Ibrahim: We also want proof of SOC2 compliance and a contact for security incidents.
07:33 Lina: I'll share the SOC2 PDF and the security contact email.
07:38 Claire: Great. So next steps recapped?
07:42 Samir: I'll send pricing sheet and SLA matrix by Monday 2026-07-20.
07:49 Marcus: We'll send consolidated redlines by 2026-07-22.
07:54 Lina: Security pack and SOC2 by 2026-07-19.
07:58 Ibrahim: I'll propose CISO call windows for the week of 7/27.
08:02 Dana: We'll send sample traffic and success criteria by 2026-07-23.
08:08 Samir: Once redlines are exchanged we'll aim to set up the Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity — provisioning typically takes 3-5 business days after PO.
08:19 Claire: Procurement will try to expedite PO; prefer net-45.
08:24 Samir: Noted. We'll include net-45 option in pricing.
08:28 Marcus: One last note — we'll share a marked-up clause for SLA credits; please review with legal.
08:34 Samir: Will do. Thanks everyone.
08:38 End of meeting.
